And shortly after, Sultan Berkyaruq went to Isfahan with a few men from his army.
And the nobles of his brother, Sultan Mahmud, closed the gates against him;
then they thought to bring him in and lay hands on him.
And when they opened to him and he entered,

and on that very day he died,
being seven years old.
And the nobles submitted to Berkyaruq,
and they made him king also over Isfahan.

Qilij Arslan, the son of Sulayman, the Sultan of Iconium, came
and encamped against Melitene,

Now a certain chief deacon who was with the Sultan
approached as an envoy, and sought to speak with the bishop of the city,
who was Sa'id bar Sabuni,
who was called Mor Yoḥanon of his sedre,
a holy man and a wondrous teacher.
And when that bishop drew near by the command of Gabriel the accursed Greek, the governor of the city,
that deacon said to him in Syriac:
"The Sultan says to you: Surrender the city,
and he will deal kindly with you;
but if not,
he will take it by the sword,
and your blood and that of all the people God will require at your hands."
The bishop, however, replied:
"Do not talk foolishly {OCR?};
this city no one is able to conquer,
by the power of God.
For there is bread in it for more than ten years,
and its water springs up and flows from within it,
and many warriors, valiant men, are in it,
even as you see."
And while he was speaking these things,
